chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Sa'id al-A'raj who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, there are women with us, so should I send them forth at night?' He said, 'Yes, you want to do as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did.' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Send them forth at night, and do not send them forth until you have made them stand at Jamm (Muzdalifah). Then send them forth until they arrive at the Great Jamrah and throw (the pebbles) at the Jamrah. If there is no sacrifice upon them, let them take from their hair and trim their nails. Then they shall proceed to Mecca with their faces (facing the Kaaba), and perform Tawaf around the House, and perform Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. Then they shall return to the House and perform another Tawaf (of seven circuits). Then they shall return to Mina, having completed their Hajj.'
And he said, 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Usamah with them.'
And we have previously presented the discussion regarding the Sa'i in Wadi Muhassir, and that is further clarified by what he narrated:

key_terms.الْجَمْرَةَ الْعُظْمَى: The Great Jamrah, the largest of the three pillars where pebbles are thrown
key_terms.جَمْعٍ: Muzdalifah, the place where pilgrims stand after sunset on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah
key_terms.طُوفْنَ بِالْبَيْتِ: They performed Tawaf (circumambulation) around the Kaaba
key_terms.وَسَعَيْنَ: And they performed Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual procedure for women during Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific ritual sequence for women during the Hajj, emphasizing their departure from Mina to Muzdalifah at night to avoid the crowds, a practice attributed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). It details the completion of the minor pilgrimage (*Hajj al-Tamattu'*) components, including stoning the Jamrah, trimming hair/nails, and performing Tawaf and Sa'i, while noting the historical precedent of Usamah ibn Zayd accompanying them. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on following the Prophet's practical guidance in managing gender-specific logistical challenges during the pilgrimage rites.
